proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to ~1200+/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), and the majority of disputed bills (59%, 1785/3025) are built on ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates (E-02); no tariff rate change occurred this year (E-04, E-07) and ticket response times remain within SLA (E-03). Together this indicates the surge is primarily driven by a non-tariff defect in the billing import/calculation step of the meter-to-cash process that produces incorrect bill amounts on correctly-read accounts, not by response-capacity backlog or by estimate substitution alone.
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled starting August 2026 (E-05/F-05).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are built on ACTUAL meter reads, not estimates (E-02/F-02).
No tariff rate change on record this year (E-04/F-04, corroborated by E-07).

causal_chain: Meter reads (AMI or manual) enter the billing import + validation step of the meter-to-cash process to produce customer bills.
A non-tariff defect in billing import/calculation logic (tariff change ruled out by E-04, E-07) produces incorrect bill amounts even on bills built from ACTUAL meter reads.
Billing-db records show 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are ACTUAL-read type, indicating miscalculation rather than estimate substitution accounts for the majority of disputes (E-02).
Customers receiving incorrect bills open dispute tickets in the CRM, which doubled from ~600/month to ~1200+/month starting August (E-05).
Ticket response times remain within SLA (E-03), confirming the surge is a billing-accuracy issue rather than a response-capacity backlog.

assumptions.statement: The ACTUAL-read billing errors originate in the billing import/calculation step of meter-to-cash rather than upstream read collection, inferred from the process definition and the ruled-out tariff change.

proposal.summary: SH-CS requested (CL-01) an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills, framing the Aug-Sep dispute doubling as a response-capacity problem. Investigation (PD-1) instead established via E-05/E-02/E-04/E-07/E-03 that volume doubled since August, 59% of disputed bills are built on ACTUAL (not estimated) reads, no tariff change occurred, and response times are within SLA — pointing to a non-tariff billing import/calculation defect as the primary driver, not ticket backlog. The release delivers two completed diagnostic correlations (disputed bills by read type/account, and route completion vs. estimated disputes) under decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no bill writes or dispatch changes made, while the CRITICAL root-cause-locating step for the ACTUAL-read majority remains blocked by an open verification obligation.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the issue as response-capacity/backlog and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills; this hypothesis (H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY) was REJECTED on E-01, E-02, E-03 since response times are within SLA.

Problem definition PD-1 (CONDITIONAL_PASS) established the surge via E-05 (volume doubled Jun-Jul ~600 to Aug-Sep ~1200+), E-02 (59%/1785 of 3025 disputed bills are ACTUAL-read, not ESTIMATED), and E-04/E-07 (zero tariff changes), concluding a non-tariff billing import/calculation defect is the primary suspected cause.

Completed work (W-WI-1, W-WI-2A, W-WI-2B) correlated disputed bills by read type/account (DA-TICKET) and route completion with estimated disputes (DA-ROUTE); this is the released scope per solution_design.release_scope.

E-12 found that for the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts, 1,184 had AMI reads received on time but rejected at billing import for high consumption, and only 56 had no AMI read at all — indicating billing-import rejection, not AMI delivery failure, dominates that minority.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: completed, non-blocked scope items ship, while VOB-U-CALC-DEFECT-LOCUS (CRITICAL, OPEN) continues to block query_billing_import_validation_rule_log:DA-RULES, so the ACTUAL-read majority root cause is not identified in this release.

No protected actions were taken: no automated or unauthorized bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) and no field dispatch route changes (K-DISPATCH) occurred; any remediation requires separate owner-authorized action by SH-BILL (per unfinished-scope item SR-BILLING-CONFIG-CORRECTION-BY, not feasible in contest time).

Underlying stakeholder claims remain unverified or disputed: SH-FIELD's staffing account (CL-02/E-06) is flagged with a possible headcount-growth incentive bias (A-SH-FIELD-BIAS) and can at most explain the ESTIMATED-read minority (A-ESTIMATE-MINORITY-SCOPE), while SH-AMI's access-provisioned claim (CL-04/E-11) is also unverified stakeholder input.
limitations_explained: The CRITICAL root cause of the ACTUAL-read majority of disputes (59%, 1785/3025 bills, E-02) is not identified in this release: query_billing_import_validation_rule_log:DA-RULES is blocked by the still-OPEN VOB-U-CALC-DEFECT-LOCUS, so the specific defective billing rule/calculation step is unconfirmed.

No bill is corrected by this release: any owner-authorized correction to the import/validation rule in DA-RULES (per SH-BILL) must happen as a separate, explicitly authorized Billing Operations action, and no automated bill write occurred, consistent with constraint K-BILLWRITE.

The route-completion/estimated-dispute correlation is descriptive, not a confirmed causal link: unknowns.U-STAFFING-CAUSAL-LINK is actually RESOLVED, but the disclosed limitations text incorrectly states it 'remains OPEN' — this is an internal inconsistency flagged by verify_completed (semantic:staffing_vob_status_inconsistency) and should be read with that caution.

A disclosed limitation claims the AMI read-event query is blocked by an OPEN VOB and a DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export, but state shows that VOB is RESOLVED, mdms-export tool_health is HEALTHY, and E-12 is the actual completed query output — this contradiction was flagged by verify_completed (semantic:ami_limitation_stale_vs_evidence) and the stale wording should not be relied upon.

Delivery and semantic validity of the H-FIELD-BILL (manual reads) and H-MDMS-BILL (AMI reads) handoffs into billing remain UNKNOWN per the CONDITIONAL define-gate findings, so handoff integrity itself is unverified even though E-12 characterizes what happens to reads once received.

SH-FIELD's staffing-shortfall claim (CL-02/E-06) carries a disclosed potential bias (incentive to grow contract headcount, A-SH-FIELD-BIAS) and, per A-ESTIMATE-MINORITY-SCOPE, can at most account for the smaller ESTIMATED-read dispute population, not the larger ACTUAL-read share.
